body:
Redline round 1

Reviewed the whole pull request.

The renumbering is complete: grep finds no stale step 10, step 11 or 'eleven' reference outside the spec folders. Point 7 keeps its 'Steps 10, 11 and 12 stay as written' sentence first, so the setup script's regexes still read the fill-ins back correctly (traced against `read_fillins` and `apply`), and the restamp is in the same commit as the gate edit. The three findings come from one source: the gate step, point 7, plan approver check 8, the new standard and the README each describe the Docs entry a little differently (when the commit is named, where the entry sits, and which step number it has).

### Findings (1 correctness, 2 nit)

- **R1-1** · nit · low · likely · `README.md:162` · README pins the Docs step to step 10, and the Docs rule will not catch it going stale
- **R1-2** · nit · low · likely · `agent-os/standards/process/docs-gate.md:7` · Standard puts Docs entries under a heading; point 7 puts them in each task
- **R1-3** · correctness · low · likely · `agents/redline-plan-approver.md:23` · Check 8 asks for a commit the plan cannot name yet

Each finding has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the finding's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, once the round's fixes are committed.

comments.body:
**R1-1** · nit · low · likely

**README pins the Docs step to step 10, and the Docs rule will not catch it going stale**

The new Contributing sentence opens "The gate's step 10 is a Docs step". Gate numbers change whenever a command step is added: #40 (bc6a18d) added step 9 and moved the retrospective from 9 to 10, and this PR's own survey found `standards-retrospective.md:5` still on the old number only by chance. Until now the README carried no gate step number (grep finds only the setup skill's own step 10 at line 269). The next spec that adds a command step will make this sentence wrong, and the Docs rule will not flag it, because a gate edit touches `.claude/commands/agent-os/shape-spec.md` and `.claude/redline/`, neither of which is on the step's directory list.

Proposed fix: Refer to the step by its title instead of its number, for example "The gate has a Docs step, after its nine command steps: ..." or "The gate's Docs step ...".

**R1-2** · nit · low · likely

**Standard puts Docs entries under a heading; point 7 puts them in each task**

The standard says the entries go 'under a "Docs entries" heading in `plan.md`'. Gate step 10 sets no location, and unattended point 7 (shape-spec.md line 44) tells the Redline shaper that 'a task that adds or alters a file ... names the README section ... it updates', which puts the entry inside each task. A shaper that carries `process/docs-gate` in `standards.md` (likely for any finding in `scripts/` or `agents/`, given its index description) gets two placements that conflict. The plan approver's check 7 holds tasks to `standards.md`, so it can bounce a plan written per point 7 for having no 'Docs entries' heading. This PR's own plan uses neither form exactly: its heading is 'Task 6: Docs entries for this spec'.

Proposed fix: Make the bullet accept both forms, for example "in `plan.md`: in the task that touches the file (a Redline round, per point 7 of the unattended section) or under a Docs entries heading (a hand-shaped spec)". Or drop the heading requirement and keep "in `plan.md`".

**R1-3** · correctness · low · likely

**Check 8 asks for a commit the plan cannot name yet**

Check 8 requires each Docs entry to give 'a README section (and template, if any) with the commit or a "no reader-facing change" reason'. The plan approver runs before the implementer, so no commit exists yet. Unattended point 7 asks the shaper only to name the README section the task updates, or to say 'no reader-facing change' and why; it never asks for a commit. A plan written exactly as point 7 says can therefore be bounced under a literal reading of check 8. The reshape prompt cannot add a real commit, and each bounce counts against `maxPlanAdjustments`, after which an unattended run goes back to the person. This PR's own plan works around the gap with placeholders ('Task 5's commit'). No such commit exists: the README edit landed in 836c4b6 together with the gate edit and both agent files.

Proposed fix: Reword check 8 to match what exists when the approver runs: "a README section (and template, if any) that the task updates, or a 'no reader-facing change' reason"; the commit is the task's own and is named when it lands. Or have point 7 tell the shaper to write "this task's commit" as the entry's commit, so the two roles agree.
